You are a senior Rust/Python performance engineer on treams-rs (T-matrix scattering: Rust core crates/treams-core, PyO3 bindings crates/treams-py -> treams_rs._native, Python API python/treams_rs). Work ONLY in the git worktree lanes/perf2 (branch lane-perf2, starting at 65b8a05 (condensed into 8251007)). HARD TIME LIMIT: finish, commit and report within 100 minutes of wall time; if a fix is not clearly working by then, stop, revert it and report the diagnosis.

GOAL (owner rule: no regressions vs the original main 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8), including speed). Two workloads of scripts/benchmark_cluster.py are still slightly slower than 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) in their BACKWARD (pullback) timing, measured with 6 interleaved CPU-time pairs, 1 thread:

  • incgamma --samples 128: backward 10.05 us (base) vs 10.53 us (head): ratio 1.055, all 6 pairs above 1.03 (forward is 0.87, fine).
  • plane-field (default args): backward 3849 us vs 3962 us: ratio ~1.034 (borderline; an earlier analysis found equal instruction counts in the native pullback, so the cost may be in Python-side glue, allocation, copies, or the floating-point guard). Find the cause and fix it without changing any numerical result (bitwise identical values and pullbacks) or any public behaviour/error message.

TOOLS: every Bash call starts in a fresh shell: cd lanes/perf2 && .... Use scratch: wt.sh: build-ext (debug), build-ext-release (release .so into python/), pytest <args>, rust-test, rust-lint, rust-fmt, py-fmt, py-lint, py-types, docs, docs-check, gates, full, parity, rust-doc. Shared venv .venv (do not pip/uv install anything). The A/B timing tool: cd P1 && .venv/bin/python ab.py --cpu 3 --pairs 6 --cputime --a base --b lanes/perf2 --out perf2_ab.jsonl -- incgamma --samples 128 (base = release build of 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) at treams (Python original): base; --b must be a tree with a release python/treams_rs/native*.so and scripts/, i.e. run wt.sh build-ext-release in perf2 first). Look at the workload definitions in scripts/benchmark_cluster.py (search 'incgamma' and 'plane-field') to see exactly which Python calls are timed (diff.incgamma(...) and its context.pullback, etc.). Compare the code path against 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) with git -C lanes/perf2 diff 5dadf1d HEAD -- <files> (now 76ed0e8) (python/treams_rs/diff.py, python/treams_rs/.py, crates/treams-py/src/.rs, crates/treams-py/src/convert.rs, residual/cotangent helpers, the fpenv ieee guard). Profile with in-process timing loops (time.perf_counter over thousands of calls) and, if useful, callgrind (valgrind is installed) on a release build. The host has 4 shared CPUs and other agents are running tests; always interleave A/B and pin with taskset. DO NOT touch crates/treams-core/src/lattice.rs, integrals.rs, special.rs, jet.rs, python/treams_rs/lattice.py, special.py (another lane owns them).

RULES: keep all tests passing; strict lints (clippy all+pedantic+nursery -D warnings, unwrap_used denied; ruff; strict pyrefly). Small signed commits (the git config signs automatically; never disable signing), conventional subject, body with before/after measurements, ending with exactly these two lines: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com Claude-Session: [link to a conversation in the cloud] Write commit messages to a file under scratch and use git commit -F. Before finishing run scratch: wt.sh full (its parity step prints FAIL only for the accepted case wigner3j_large_j100_30_m99_-30; anything else failing is yours) and scratch: wt.sh rust-doc, then rm -rf target/release to save disk (rebuild the debug extension with wt.sh build-ext if full needs it). git status must be clean at the end.

REPORT (final message): per workload the before/after A/B ratios vs base (forward and backward), the cause found, commits (sha + subject), verification results, and anything left unresolved.

Both workloads are now faster than 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) in backward, as well as forward. Values and pullbacks are unchanged bit for bit. Two signed commits on lane-perf2 in lanes/perf2 (on top of 65b8a05 (condensed into 8251007)). Only crates/treams-core/src/broadcast.rs and plane.rs were changed; the other lane's files were not touched. It took about 53 minutes, so well inside the limit.

A/B vs base 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) (ab.py, 6 interleaved CPU-time pairs, 1 thread, taskset CPU 3, last run on the committed release build):

Workload Direction Before After
incgamma --samples 128 backward 1.055 0.937 (pair median 0.933, earlier runs 0.954 and 0.931)
incgamma --samples 128 forward 0.87 0.863
plane-field (default args) backward ~1.034 0.918 (pair median 0.916, earlier runs 0.929, 0.918, 0.931; almost every pair below 0.96)
plane-field (default args) forward — 0.89–0.93
plane-operator (shares the plane code) backward — 0.73–0.78

Causes

  1. incgamma. 65b8a05 (condensed into 8251007) moved the gamma pullback onto broadcast::pullback, which added two costs:

    • It collected a Vec<[Complex; A]> and then copied each argument's column into a new vector: an extra allocation and pass on every call.
    • broadcast::map called rayon::current_num_threads() on every call. That starts rayon's global pool, so even small in-order evaluations left an idle worker thread in the process. A dummy idle thread alone slowed the pullback by about 1.5% in process.

    In-process timing (p10 of batched pullbacks) went base 8.70 us, before 9.11 us, after 8.21 us. Callgrind instruction counts were not the issue: head already ran slightly fewer instructions than base.

  2. plane-field. The per-mode contraction became a closure shared by the in-order and parallel folds. LLVM stopped inlining it into rayon's fold helper, and each sample then recomputed checked g[(3p+a, column)] offsets and updated result.*[..] accumulators through memory. With about the same instruction count it ran roughly 1% slower in process (3–3.5% in the harness). The fix walks the cotangent column as [Complex; 3] rows alongside the points and their gradients, and keeps the accumulators in local references. Every term and addition stays in the same order. In process: base 3.79 ms, before 3.83 ms, after 3.45 ms.

Commits

  • e0d404e (condensed into 8251007) perf: pull back elementwise kernels without intermediates on one thread
    • When the pullback runs in order, gradients are pushed directly, and scalar-argument sums start from zero and add in output order, exactly as Iterator::sum does.
    • The rayon thread count is read only for a chunked evaluation that reaches its threshold.
    • The broadcast proptest now asserts exact equality across all schedules instead of a 1e-12 tolerance.
  • 08bc591 (condensed into 8251007) perf: contract plane-field cotangents without per-sample index math

Verification

  • Bitwise checks, plane-field: 256 pullback outputs match a release build of the pre-change code exactly, with 1 and 4 threads. They cover sizes on both sides of the parallel threshold, propagating and evanescent waves, weighted and operator, fixed and free vectors, helicity and parity.
  • Bitwise reasoning, broadcast: the order-preserving sum argument above, plus the exact-equality test.
  • Gates:
    • wt.sh full passes all gates: fmt, clippy with -D warnings, 199 core tests, ruff, pyrefly, docs-check.
    • pytest: 4389 passed, 36 skipped, 2 xfailed.
    • Parity: the only FAIL is the accepted wigner3j_large_j100_30_m99_-30.
    • wt.sh rust-doc passes.
  • Cleanup: target/release removed and git status is clean. The commits carry SSH signatures; git log %G? shows N only because allowedSignersFile isn't configured.

Unresolved, outside the assignment

  • incgamma at the default 2048 samples, backward: about 1.07 vs base. This already exists at 65b8a05 (condensed into 8251007) (base → 65b8a05 (condensed into 8251007) measured 1.069); my changes leave it about unchanged (65b8a05 (condensed into 8251007) → head 0.997 in A/B, slightly faster in process). This size takes the parallel path. Part of the gap is probably the column copy that path still makes, but I didn't pursue it for scope and time.
  • bessel --samples 128, backward: base → 65b8a05 (condensed into 8251007) is 1.006–1.014 and my changes leave it unchanged (in-process p10 is identical), so this looks fine.

Scratch files are in perf2, including reference trees ref65 (65b8a05 (condensed into 8251007) release) and final (08bc591 (condensed into 8251007) release) for re-running the A/B. They can be deleted. A/B records were appended to perf2_ab.jsonl.

incgamma backward at the default 2048 samples is now below base 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8), where it was about 1.07x. Values and pullbacks are unchanged bit for bit under every schedule. One signed commit on lane-perf2 in lanes/perf2 (on top of 08bc591 (condensed into 8251007)); only crates/treams-core/src/broadcast.rs changed. It took about 22 minutes of the 60.

A/B vs 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) (ab.py, 6 interleaved CPU-time pairs, 1 thread, taskset CPU 3):

Workload Direction Before After (committed build)
incgamma, 2048 samples backward 1.07 0.952 (pair median 0.955; earlier runs 0.962 and 0.982)
incgamma, 2048 samples forward — 0.878
incgamma --samples 4096 backward — 0.974 (pair median 0.980; earlier run 0.985, pairs 0.95–1.01)
incgamma --samples 4096 forward — 0.89
incgamma --samples 128 backward — 0.927 (in-order path, not changed by this commit)
incgamma --samples 128 forward — 0.889

In-process p10 per pullback at 2048 samples:

Threads 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) Before After
1 140–142 us 148–151 us 135–136 us
4 (RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4, wall time) 118–126 us 134–179 us 108–117 us

The 4-thread harness A/B was too noisy on the shared host to rank (pair ratios 0.25–4.3). Its medians were 0.870 by CPU time and 0.982 by wall time, and the in-process numbers above are the dependable figure.

Cause

  • The parallel path of broadcast::pullback collected Result<[Complex; A]> items through rayon's fallible collect. That collect gathers partial vectors in a linked list before appending them.
  • It then copied every argument's column into a vector of its own.
  • Callgrind (1 thread, incgamma at 2048) put the pullback at 1.395M instructions against base's 1.347M. Nearly all of the extra was in the per-element rayon helper (+41k) and the column copy (+6k).

Fix

  • The parallel path now writes each output's argument cotangents into a preallocated row. It uses an indexed try_for_each over rows, cotangent and index, with the same minimum chunk length.
  • A single array argument takes the rows as its gradient with no copy (Vec::into_flattened).
  • Otherwise the columns are gathered as before, and a scalar argument's terms still add in output order.
  • The pullback is now 1.314M instructions per call.

Commit

  • 078ac28 (condensed into 8251007) perf: fill parallel elementwise pullbacks in place

Verification

  • Bitwise: I compared 649 values and pullbacks between the previous build (08bc591 (condensed into 8251007)) and the new one. They cover incgamma (scalar and array degree), intkambe (3 broadcast patterns), wigner (1 and 3 arguments), bessel (with and without derivative), the 4 angular kinds, spherical and cylindrical translations, and vsw/vcw/vsh waves. Each runs at 11 sizes on both sides of every threshold (1 to 4096). All match exactly with 1 and 4 threads, and the 1-thread and 4-thread results also match each other.
  • Errors: error types and messages are unchanged (singular derivative, non-finite cotangent, residual already consumed).
  • Proptest: kept on exact equality, and extended with a single-argument pullback under all schedules.
  • Other workloads vs 08bc591 (condensed into 8251007) (backward A/B):
    • bessel --samples 128: 0.961
    • wigner: 0.931
    • intkambe: 0.997. Callgrind shows 0.4% more instructions here, but it is still about 45% below 5dadf1d (now 76ed0e8) (8.42M vs 15.16M).
  • Gates:
    • wt.sh full passes all gates, including 199 core tests.
    • pytest: 4389 passed, 36 skipped, 2 xfailed.
    • Parity: the only FAIL is the accepted wigner3j_large_j100_30_m99_-30.
    • wt.sh rust-doc passes.
  • Cleanup: target/release removed, git status clean, and the commit carries its SSH signature.

Unresolved: nothing open. Scratch files are in perf2; the reference trees final (08bc591 (condensed into 8251007)) and final3 (078ac28 (condensed into 8251007) release) can be deleted. A/B records were appended to perf2_ab.jsonl.
